result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.expand_seed_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Expand a seed set to a connected module using neighborhood scoring. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.expand_seed_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Expand a seed set to a connected module using neighborhood scoring. title: >- [Graph.expand_seed_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Expand a seed set to a connected module using neighborhood scoring. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Expand a seed set to a connected module using neighborhood scoring. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L69009-L69110){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.expand_seed_set( seeds, max_size=None, min_score=0.0, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Expand a seed set into a module](../assets/graphs/expand-seed-set.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with the seeds A and B outlined and the two nodes the expansion adds, C and D, filled in accent, all four inside a shaded module. Each joins with 2 of its 3 edges into the module, a score of 2/3, and the size cap of 4 stops the growth before E. The card returns A, B, C, D." width="100%"} Starting from seed nodes, greedily adds neighbors that are densely connected to the current module. The score for each candidate is the ratio of its edges to the module over its total degree, favoring nodes tightly linked to the module rather than high-degree hubs. At each step the highest-scoring neighbor of the module is added, and the scores are recomputed. Growth stops when the module reaches `max_size=` nodes, when the best candidate's score is not above `min_score=`, or when the module has no outside neighbors left. This kind of seed expansion is common when you know a few "anchor" nodes and want the local neighborhood that belongs with them: - growing a disease module from a handful of known disease genes in an interaction network - finding the community around a set of users or accounts of interest - building a focused subgraph for visualization or downstream analysis Because a candidate's score is penalized by its degree, a hub with many edges outside the module scores low even if it touches the module, while a node whose few edges all lead into the module scores high (up to `1.0`). Since every node that touches the module has a positive score, the default `min_score=0.0` accepts any neighbor, so the module simply grows until it hits `max_size=`; raise `min_score=` to keep only well-integrated nodes. When several candidates tie for the best score, which one is added first is arbitrary. On directed graphs only outgoing edges are considered, both for finding candidates and for computing degree. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [seeds]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int | str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of seed nodes, as integer IDs or string labels (the two can be mixed). All seeds are included in the result. At least one seed is required, and every one must exist in the graph. [max_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of nodes in the final module, seeds included. If `None` (the default), the limit is three times the number of distinct seeds. If `max_size=` is not larger than the number of seeds, no nodes are added. [min_score]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum connectivity score for a node to be added. A candidate is added only if its score (edges into the module divided by its degree) is strictly greater than this value, so candidates scoring at or below the threshold are rejected and expansion stops. Default is `0.0`, which accepts any neighbor of the module. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node IDs of the expanded module (seeds included), sorted in ascending order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `seeds=` is empty or any seed node doesn't exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two seeds share a tightly linked neighbor `T` (all of its edges go to the seeds) and a `Hub` that is mostly connected to outside nodes. With `min_score=0.3`, `T` joins with a score of `1.0`, but the hub's score of `1/4` is too low, so expansion stops there: ::: {#a2975d55 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["S1", "S2", "T", "Hub", "X", "Y", "Z"]) .add_edges( [ ("S1", "S2"), ("S1", "T"), ("S2", "T"), ("S1", "Hub"), ("Hub", "X"), ("Hub", "Y"), ("Hub", "Z"), ] ) ) module = graph.expand_seed_set(seeds=["S1", "S2"], min_score=0.3) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in module] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['S1', 'S2', 'T'] ``` ::: ::: With the default `min_score=0.0`, any neighbor is accepted and only `max_size=` limits growth. Capping the module at 4 nodes adds `T` first (highest score) and then the hub: ::: {#d960d544 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} module = graph.expand_seed_set(seeds=["S1", "S2"], max_size=4) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in module] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['S1', 'S2', 'T', 'Hub'] ``` ::: :::
